The user wants to get object descriptors related to a domain example.org on VirusTotal. They want to check the relationship "subdomains". They want just the related object's IDs (and context attributes, if any) instead of returning all attributes. They provide their API key "my_api". They want to set limit to 10 and continuation cursor to abc.

We need to call the VirusTotal API. The user didn't specify the exact endpoint. But we can guess: For retrieving related objects, we might use the endpoint: GET /domains/{domain}/related_objects?relationship=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc. The API key is passed via header or query param. Usually it's via header: x-apikey: <key>.

We need to produce a JSON request body? Actually for GET requests, we don't have a body. We need to produce a request with method GET, URL, headers, query parameters. The user wants us to do that. So we need to produce a JSON object with fields: method, url, headers, query_params. No body. Then we need to call the tool. The tool expects a JSON with fields: method, url, headers, query_params, body. Body can be omitted or null.

We need to produce the request. Let's construct:

method: GET
url: https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/related_objects
headers: { "x-apikey": "my_api" }
query_params: { "relationship": "subdomains", "limit": "10", "continuation_cursor": "abc" }

We need to pass this to the tool. The tool will then call the API. The response will be returned. We need to output the response from the tool. The tool returns a JSON with fields: status_code, headers, body. We need to output that. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we just output the tool's response.
